polityNote: People’s Republic of China, province-level units 1949-10-01 → 1979-06-30 (the 1979-07-01 restoration of Inner Mongolia is where CHN.json, on Natural Earth, takes over). Atoms: geoBoundaries CHN ADM3 (OpenStreetMap county-level units of 2017, ODbL). A province is drawn on a span only when every stretch of its outline then is a line of today’s county-level units: the complete year-by-year record of 区划地名网 (xzqh.org, province pages 1949–2019, which record village- and commune-level transfers between provinces with the approving document and day) was read for all 31 provinces, and a province is drawn only from the day after the last transfer across its line that is recorded anywhere up to 2019 (unions also absorb later whole-county moves: Beijing 1958, Tianjin 1973, the 1969–79 Inner Mongolia split, Qinzhou 1965). Every province had sub-county transfers in the 1950s, so nothing is drawn before 1958. Withheld throughout: Jiangsu and Shandong (Weishan 1984), Anhui and Hubei (Jinzhai forest 1984), Sichuan and Guizhou (Qijiang–Xishui 1979), Guangxi and Yunnan (China–Vietnam line 1999/2009), Heilongjiang (Bolshoy Ussuriysky 2008), Tibet (atoms include Arunachal Pradesh), Xinjiang (1994–2011 treaties). Boundary-survey agreements that fix a disputed line without moving land are listed, not withheld (same practice as CHN.json). Hong Kong and Macau atoms are outside; Kinmen, Matsu and Taiwan carry no atom in this set. Independent check (2026-10-06): against the OpenHistoricalMap records of the same units in 1965, clipped to land, the drawn Zhejiang has IoU 0.9985 (103,890 vs 103,901 km²) and Shanghai 0.9963 (7,024 vs 7,029 km²); where OHM answers, the builder keeps the OHM record. Drawn areas against the atoms’ own Natural Earth provinces differ by 0–4% (Natural Earth generalisation).
